paper.title_en: Penrose process in radiating Kerr-Vaidya black holes: efficiency, energy transport, and the viability boundary
paper.abstract_en: We study single-particle Penrose extraction from a rotating black hole whose mass decreases in time, described by the ingoing Kerr-Vaidya metric, imposing exact four-momentum conservation at the decay. We prove that the local efficiency is bounded by the instantaneous Kerr value, through a covariant bound that reduces to the Bardeen-Press-Teukolsky limit at the horizon, and we derive an exact transport law, dE/dtau = -dm/dt (r/Sigma) p_r^2 for fixed spin parameter, by which every timelike geodesic gains energy while the hole loses mass. The net energy gain therefore splits into a local Penrose term and two transport terms, which we compute numerically as functions of spin and mass-loss rate for two mass-loss laws. With fixed spin parameter, extraction is possible only below a critical rate alpha_crit(a) = (M-a)/Delta v, set by the approach of the hole to extremality; with fixed a/m no such boundary exists. The transport law extends to the Kerr-Newman-Vaidya family, and the regime where the dynamics matter is shown to lie far outside astrophysical mass-loss rates.
